chunks: From him, from Fudayla, from Aban, from Salama, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came to Safwan ibn Umayya and asked him for weapons, eighty breastplates. Safwan asked him, 'As a loan (ariyyah) that is guaranteed (dhaminah), or as a seizure (ghasb)?' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'No, as a loan that is guaranteed.' Safwan said, 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between ariyyah and ghasb in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith highlights the Prophet’s (SAW) pragmatic approach to resource management during military campaigns, specifically borrowing armor from Safwan ibn Umayya. It establishes the legal distinction between a voluntary loan (*'ariyyah*) with guaranteed liability (*dhaminah*) and forced seizure (*ghasb*), a foundational concept in Shia jurisprudence for understanding property rights and trust. The narration underscores the Prophet’s adherence to contractual clarity and mutual consent even when acquiring items from prominent companions.
